one_sentence: This paper proves that a parity-breaking cubic term in the moral-sector Lagrangian yields irreversible yet conserved moral cost via Noether's theorem.
executive_summary: This document presents the formal proof of Law 9: moral cost is both irreversible and conserved. It constructs a moral-sector Lagrangian with a parity-breaking cubic term, applies Noether's theorem to derive the conserved charge Q_m, and shows that the cubic term cancels identically in the conservation proof. The three-body decay model (wholeness → broken state + visible damage + invisible remainder) mirrors muon decay kinematics, with the invisible remainder ν_loss carrying displaced cost. Grace is introduced as an open-system source term that can reverse entropy production through atonement. The proof is verified in Lean and depends on earlier pages establishing Lagrangian structure and conservation framework.
short_summary: This document is the formal proof of Law 9, showing that moral cost is both irreversible and conserved. The core structural claim is that a parity-breaking cubic term in the Lagrangian produces irreversibility without breaking Noether conservation. Key evidence is the explicit derivation showing the cubic term cancels out of the time-derivative of the conserved charge. This matters because it establishes the mathematical foundation for atonement as an external source term that can close the moral ledger.
